html:
The Apache are several related peoples of the American Southwest, the southern Plains and northern Mexico. They speak Southern Athabaskan languages, close to that of the Navajo.

Their ancestors were Athabaskan hunters who came south from western Canada, arriving in the Southwest between about 1000 and 1500. They split into many independent bands, among them the Chiricahua, Western Apache, Mescalero, Jicarilla and Lipan. Their homeland of mountains, canyons, deserts and plains was called Apachería.

They traded and fought with the Pueblo towns, and from the late 1600s raided the frontier of New Spain for horses and cattle. In the 1700s the Comanche pushed them off the southern plains. Wars with Mexico and then the United States went on until 1886, when Geronimo surrendered. Apache tribes today have reservations in Arizona, New Mexico and Oklahoma.
sum: The Apache are several related peoples of the American Southwest, the southern Plains and northern Mexico. They speak Southern Athabaskan languages, close to that of the Navajo.
